youtube.title: We Cooked Crystals and the Cops Showed Up
youtube.description:
The wizard and Nyx cooked crystals. The police had questions. It was rock candy.

Hot water near boiling can hold almost five times its own weight in sugar. Let it cool and it holds more than it should (supersaturated), so the extra sugar crystallises on a rough string over about a week, in flat-sided crystals because the molecules stack in a repeating pattern. And crack a sugar crystal in a really dark room: it gives off faint flashes of light (triboluminescence).

No crimes were committed. Only candy.

Sources:
- CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Aqueous solubility of sucrose' (487 g per 100 g water at 100 °C, 204 g at 20 °C).
- Exploratorium, 'Rock Candy' science snack.
- L. M. Sweeting et al., 'Triboluminescence with and without air', Chemistry of Materials 13, 854-870 (2001).

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs). The flashes are drawn brighter than real life so they show on a phone.

Counterphysical: physics that breaks your intuition.

#shorts #science #chemistry #rockcandy #crystals #funny #comedy
